question.prompt: Consider the set of complex numbers \(z\) satisfying \(|1+z+z^2|=4.\) The maximum value of the imaginary part of \(z\) can be written in the form \(\dfrac{\sqrt{m}}{n},\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are relatively prime positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.title: Complete the square and bound
solutions.explanation:
Completing the square introduces a horizontal shift, which preserves the imaginary part and allows a direct modulus bound.

Let \(w=z+\tfrac12\). Then
\[
1+z+z^2=w^2+\frac34,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\left|w^2+\frac34\right|=4.
\]
The modulus of a product is the product of the moduli, so \(|w^2|=|w|^2\). Applying the triangle inequality gives
\[
|w|^2
=\left|\left(w^2+\frac34\right)-\frac34\right|
\le\left|w^2+\frac34\right|+\frac34
=\frac{19}{4}.
\]
A complex number's imaginary part is at most its modulus. Because \(w\) and \(z\) have the same imaginary part, this proves
\[
\operatorname{Im}z\le |w|\le\frac{\sqrt{19}}2.
\]
The bound is attained by taking
\[
w=\frac{\sqrt{19}}2i,
\qquad z=-\frac12+\frac{\sqrt{19}}2i.
\]
Indeed, \(w^2+\tfrac34=-\tfrac{19}{4}+\tfrac34=-4\), whose modulus is \(4\).

Thus the maximum imaginary part is \(\sqrt{19}/2\). Since \(19\) and \(2\) are relatively prime, \(m+n=\boxed{21}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutions.title: Bound the two factor distances
solutions.explanation:
Factoring the quadratic turns its modulus into a product of two distances. Each distance is at least the corresponding vertical separation, which will bound the imaginary part.

The quadratic formula gives the roots of \(z^2+z+1=0\) as
\[
\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1-4}}2
=-\frac12\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1+z+z^2
=\left(z+\frac12-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i\right)
\left(z+\frac12+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}i\right).
\]
Write \(z=x+yi\), where \(x,y\) are real. Taking moduli and using \(|a+bi|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\ge |b|\), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
4
&=\sqrt{\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\left(y-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2}
\sqrt{\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\left(y+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2}\\
&\ge\left|y-\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right|
\left|y+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}\right|
=\left|y^2-\frac34\right|.
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, \(y^2-\tfrac34\le4\), so
\[
y^2\le\frac{19}{4},
\qquad y\le\frac{\sqrt{19}}2.
\]
Taking \(x=-\tfrac12\) and \(y=\sqrt{19}/2\) makes both distance inequalities equalities, and their product is \(y^2-\tfrac34=4\). Thus this value is attainable.

The maximum is \(\sqrt{19}/2\), so \(m+n=19+2=\boxed{21}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
